name: Salmeterol
route_note: Dry-powder or metered-dose inhaler twice daily, usually combined with an inhaled corticosteroid

discovery.by: Glaxo team led by David Jack
discovery.note: A salbutamol derivative with a long lipophilic side chain intended to anchor the molecule near the beta2 receptor for prolonged action.

tagline: Twice-daily long-acting bronchodilator, mainly used with fluticasone
summary: Salmeterol is a long-acting beta2-agonist that keeps airways open for about 12 hours. It is used for maintenance treatment of asthma (only together with an inhaled corticosteroid) and COPD, most often in the fluticasone/salmeterol combination inhaler.
mechanism: Like salbutamol, salmeterol activates airway beta2-adrenergic receptors, increasing cAMP and relaxing bronchial smooth muscle.

Its long lipophilic tail partitions into the cell membrane and interacts with an exosite near the receptor, allowing repeated activation and a duration of about 12 hours. The onset is slower (10–20 minutes) than that of salbutamol or formoterol, so it is not used for acute relief.
uses: Maintenance treatment of asthma in combination with an inhaled corticosteroid

history.title: UK launch
history.detail: Glaxo launches Serevent in the UK.

history.title: Advair
history.detail: FDA approves fluticasone propionate/salmeterol (Advair Diskus); marketed as Seretide outside the US.

history.title: SMART trial and boxed warning
history.detail: The Salmeterol Multicenter Asthma Research Trial reports excess asthma-related deaths with salmeterol, reinforcing an FDA boxed warning for LABAs.

history.title: LABA restrictions
history.detail: FDA requires that LABAs in asthma be used only with an asthma controller such as an inhaled corticosteroid.

history.title: Boxed warning removed for combinations
history.detail: After large safety trials of ICS/LABA combinations, FDA removes the boxed warning from ICS/LABA combination labels.

history.title: First generic Advair
history.detail: FDA approves Wixela Inhub (Mylan), the first generic fluticasone/salmeterol inhaler.

serious: Asthma-related death when used without an inhaled corticosteroid

facts: Salmeterol monotherapy is not recommended in asthma; it should be combined with an inhaled corticosteroid.
Fluticasone/salmeterol (Advair/Seretide) was for years one of GSK's best-selling medicines.
